doc.title: Lonnie Liston Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 9, 2021

title: Critics and the stretching-out sections
summary: Critics said he was banging or putting people to sleep; he says it was pure sound modeled on nature.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: Have you ever had critics or journalists say something about your music that you read, and going that wasn’t the idea at all? Or something along those lines?

Oh yeah that’ might happen. Because I remember back then I would play “A Garden of Peace” and some people would say you’re putting me to sleep. Years later. Yeah, okay. But you know oh, a lot of times they said, when we were stretching out and I was using my fingers and my things to get more sound
then you come out of it

so but they said well you know you were banging while you were — like you say I’ll use your word, when things got strange — but it was nothing like that. Either you were banging or you were frustrated and you were getting all that frustration out — that had nothing to do with it, we were just pure sound and you were expanding and then — because I mean like when you go out, and that’s why I love nature, you hear all these sounds, the birds and the water and the wind blowing through the trees and then, I mean all that’s music. You know so I was just trying to be natural and naturistic.
